name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q01 - Basic animal tissues and cardiac composition

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: All complex animals consist of only four basic types of tissues: epithelial, connective, muscular, and neural.

Statement II: The vertebrate heart is an organ composed of all four basic types of tissues.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Tissue Diversity
In all complex multicellular animals, structural organization is based on four fundamental tissue categories: epithelial tissue, connective tissue, muscular tissue, and neural tissue. Thus, the proposition regarding the four basic tissue types is factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Cardiac Tissue Architecture
The heart is a vital muscular organ whose structural framework integrates endocardial/epicardial epithelium, myocardial muscle, fibrous connective support, and regulatory neural conduction networks, incorporating all four primary tissue classes. Thus, the proposition regarding cardiac tissue composition is factually accurate.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
Both the first and second statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q02 - Morphological features of adult frog regions

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The body of an adult frog is distinctly divided into head, neck, trunk, and tail.

Statement II: Frogs actively drink water through their mouth several times a day to maintain hydration.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Body Segmentation
The body of an adult frog is streamlined and divisible only into head and trunk; both a neck and an external tail are completely absent in the adult stage. Thus, the proposition attributing four body regions including a neck and tail is factually false.

Step 2: Evaluation of Hydration Physiology
Frogs never drink liquid water orally; instead, their thin, vascularized, and mucous-coated integument allows direct osmotic absorption of moisture from the environment. Thus, the proposition claiming active oral water ingestion is factually false.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
Both the first and second statements are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q03 - Digit numbers on frog limbs comparison

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The forelimbs of a frog terminate in four digits, whereas the hindlimbs terminate in five digits.

Statement II: The digits of both forelimbs and hindlimbs possess extensive webbed skin folds for swimming.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Digit Numbers
Morphological examination of the limbs of an adult frog shows four clawless digits on each forelimb and five clawless digits on each hindlimb. Thus, the proposition regarding limb digit count is factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Webbing Location
Webbing is an adaptation for aquatic locomotion formed by cutaneous skin folds between digits, but it is restricted exclusively to the feet of the hindlimbs; the forelimb digits are entirely free and non-webbed. Thus, the proposition claiming webbing on both limb pairs is factually false.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The first statement is correct, but the second statement is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q04 - Camouflage ability and seasonal shelter burrows

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Frogs possess the physiological ability to change their skin colouration to conceal themselves from enemies, an adaptation called mimicry or camouflage.

Statement II: Frogs take shelter in deep subterranean burrows to undergo aestivation during peak summer and hibernation during peak winter.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Protective Pigmentation
Frogs adjust their skin hue between grasses and dry ground to blend with the substrate, using chromatic camouflage (protective mimicry) to evade detection by predators. Thus, the proposition regarding colour alteration is factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Thermoregulatory Dormancy
As cold-blooded poikilotherms lacking internal thermoregulation, frogs burrow into moist subterranean substrates to undergo summer sleep (aestivation) and winter sleep (hibernation). Thus, the proposition regarding seasonal burrowing dormancy is factually accurate.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
Both the first and second statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q05 - Herbivorous diet and intestinal villi distribution

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The alimentary canal of an adult frog is elongated because frogs are obligate herbivores requiring extensive cellulose fermentation.

Statement II: Final absorption of digested nutrients in frogs occurs exclusively across the muscular wall of the stomach.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Alimentary Length and Diet
Adult frogs feed on insects and small invertebrates (carnivores), meaning their digestive tract does not process cellulose; consequently, their intestine is reduced in length and the alimentary canal is relatively short. Thus, the proposition asserting an elongated herbivorous canal is factually false.

Step 2: Evaluation of Nutrient Absorption Site
Nutrient absorption takes place in the small intestine across numerous microscopic finger-like folds termed villi and microvilli, whereas the stomach functions primarily in chemical acid-peptic digestion. Thus, the proposition designating the stomach as the exclusive absorptive site is factually false.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
Both the first and second statements are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q06 - Duodenal secretions and common bile duct

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The duodenum of a frog receives bile from the gall bladder and pancreatic juice from the pancreas through a common bile duct.

Statement II: Bile secreted by the liver contains proteolytic enzymes that hydrolyze proteins into amino acids.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Duodenal Ducts
Partially digested chyme passes from the stomach into the duodenum, which receives hepatic bile and pancreatic juice through a single common hepatopancreatic duct. Thus, the proposition regarding common bile duct delivery is factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Bile Function
Bile contains bile pigments and bile salts that physically emulsify fats into micro-droplets, completely lacking digestive enzymes; enzymatic protein and carbohydrate digestion is mediated by pancreatic and intestinal enzymes. Thus, the proposition attributing proteolytic enzymatic activity to bile is factually false.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The first statement is correct, but the second statement is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q07 - Pulmonary respiration mechanisms in terrestrial frogs

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: During aquatic submersion, frogs utilize their pair of elongated pink sac-like lungs for gaseous exchange.

Statement II: On land, frogs can utilize the buccal cavity, skin, and lungs as respiratory surfaces.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Aquatic Respiratory Organs
Under water, the lungs remain non-functional and cutaneous respiration through the moist skin is the sole mechanism of gaseous exchange by simple diffusion. Thus, the proposition claiming aquatic lung breathing is factually false.

Step 2: Evaluation of Terrestrial Respiratory Routes
When dwelling on land, an adult frog has three active respiratory modes: buccopharyngeal respiration through the buccal lining, cutaneous respiration across the moist skin, and pulmonary respiration via the lungs. Thus, the proposition regarding the three terrestrial respiratory surfaces is factually accurate.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, but the second statement is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q08 - Cardiac sinus venosus and conus arteriosus

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a frog, the triangular sinus venosus joins the right atrium and receives deoxygenated blood through the major venae cavae.

Statement II: The single muscular ventricle of the frog heart opens into a sac-like conus arteriosus located on the ventral surface.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Sinus Venosus Anatomy
The sinus venosus is a prominent, thin-walled triangular chamber situated dorsally that joins the right atrium to deliver systemic venous blood collected by the venae cavae. Thus, the proposition regarding sinus venosus connectivity is factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Conus Arteriosus Anatomy
The thick-walled single ventricle directs pressurized blood through its outflow tract into the tubular, sac-like conus arteriosus situated ventrally on the heart before splitting into arterial trunks. Thus, the proposition regarding conus arteriosus orientation is factually accurate.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
Both the first and second statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q09 - Erythrocyte enucleation and lymphatic fluid composition

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Erythrocytes in the blood of an adult frog are circular, biconcave, and devoid of a nucleus at maturity.

Statement II: Lymph in frogs is identical in composition to whole blood and contains abundant erythrocytes.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Red Blood Cell Cytology
Unlike mammals, the red blood cells (erythrocytes) of frogs are oval, biconvex, and retain their nucleus throughout their functional lifespan. Thus, the proposition describing enucleated biconcave erythrocytes is factually false.

Step 2: Evaluation of Lymphatic Fluid Constituents
Lymph is a filtered interstitial fluid collected by lymphatic channels; it lacks red blood cells (erythrocytes) and contains significantly lower protein levels than blood plasma. Thus, the proposition equating lymph to whole blood is factually false.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
Both the first and second statements are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q10 - Cranial nerves count and hindbrain continuity

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: There are exactly ten pairs of cranial nerves originating from the brain of a frog.

Statement II: The medulla oblongata of the frog terminates blindly within the cranium without connecting to the spinal cord.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Cranial Nerve Quantity
The peripheral nervous system of amphibians features precisely 10 pairs of cranial nerves emerging from various regions of the brain. Thus, the proposition stating ten cranial nerve pairs is factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Medullary Extension
The posterior segment of the hindbrain, the medulla oblongata, passes out of the cranium through the foramen magnum and directly continues into the spinal cord enclosed by the vertebral column. Thus, the proposition claiming blind intra-cranial termination is factually false.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The first statement is correct, but the second statement is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q11 - Secondary sexual dimorphism features in frogs

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Sound-producing vocal sacs and copulatory nuptial pads are prominent morphological features present exclusively in female frogs.

Statement II: Male frogs can be distinguished morphologically by the presence of a copulatory pad on the first digit of each forelimb.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Female Sexual Characteristics
Sound-amplifying vocal sacs and copulatory pads are diagnostic secondary sexual structures developed only in male frogs, being completely absent in females. Thus, the proposition attributing vocal sacs and copulatory pads to females is factually false.

Step 2: Evaluation of Male Forelimb Modifications
Male frogs possess a thickened, glandular copulatory (nuptial) pad on the ventral base of the first digit of each forelimb, which aids in clasping the female during amplexus. Thus, the proposition regarding the male forelimb copulatory pad is factually accurate.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, but the second statement is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q12 - Portal systems connecting digestive and excretory organs

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In frogs, a specialized venous connection called the hepatic portal system exists between the intestine and the liver.

Statement II: A distinct renal portal system provides a specialized venous connection between the lower parts of the body and the kidneys in frogs.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Hepatic Portal Circulation
The vascular system of amphibians includes a well-defined hepatic portal vein that collects nutrient-rich venous blood from the alimentary canal (especially the intestine) and delivers it into the hepatic sinusoidal network. Thus, the proposition concerning the hepatic portal system is factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Renal Portal Circulation
Venous blood returning from the hindlimbs and pelvic region is channeled into the renal portal veins to enter the renal capillary bed before draining into the postcaval vein. Thus, the proposition concerning the renal portal system is factually accurate.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
Both the first and second statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q13 - Male and female cloacal duct configurations

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In female frogs, the ureters and oviducts fuse into a single common urinogenital duct before opening into the cloaca.

Statement II: In male frogs, the ureters transport only urine, while spermatozoa are discharged through distinct ejaculatory ducts directly to the exterior.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Female Urinogenital Ducts
In female frogs, the urinary and reproductive tracts remain completely separate: the paired ureters and the paired oviducts open independently and separately into the cloacal cavity. Thus, the proposition claiming duct fusion in females is factually false.

Step 2: Evaluation of Male Urinogenital Ducts
In male frogs, spermatozoa enter Bidder's canal in the kidneys and discharge into the ureters; consequently, the male ureters function as combined urinogenital ducts that carry both urine and sperm into the cloaca. Thus, the proposition claiming isolated urinary transport by male ureters is factually false.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
Both the first and second statements are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q14 - Male gonadal mesorchium and Bidders canal

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The yellowish ovoid testes of a male frog are suspended and attached to the upper part of the kidneys by a double fold of peritoneum called the mesorchium.

Statement II: Vasa efferentia arising from the testes bypass the kidneys completely and open directly into the urinary bladder.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Testicular Peritoneal Attachment
In male frogs, each testis is anchored to the anterior ventral surface of the corresponding kidney by a double-layered peritoneal fold termed the mesorchium. Thus, the proposition concerning the mesorchium is factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Vasa Efferentia Route
The 10 to 12 vasa efferentia emerging from each testis penetrate into the medial margin of the adjacent kidney to empty into the longitudinal Bidder's canal, communicating with the urinogenital duct rather than the urinary bladder. Thus, the proposition claiming direct bladder opening is factually false.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The first statement is correct, but the second statement is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q15 - Ovarian renal relationship and fecundity count

questiontext.text:

Statement I: The paired ovaries of a female frog possess direct internal tubular channels that communicate functionally with the renal nephrons.

Statement II: A mature female frog can lay approximately 2500 to 3000 ova at a time during external oviposition in water.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Ovarian-Renal Architecture
Although the lobed ovaries are situated adjacent to the kidneys in the coelomic cavity, there is absolutely no anatomical or functional connection between the ovaries and the renal parenchyma or tubules. Thus, the proposition claiming internal communication with nephrons is factually false.

Step 2: Evaluation of Oviposition Fecundity
During the breeding season, a mature female discharges a clutch numbering between 2500 and 3000 eggs into the water for external fertilisation. Thus, the proposition regarding egg count is factually accurate.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, but the second statement is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q16 - Sensory organ hierarchy and balance mechanisms

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a frog, the sensory papillae and taste buds represent well-organised anatomical organs, whereas eyes and internal ears are simple cellular aggregations.

Statement II: The acoustic-vestibular organ of the frog functions both in receiving sound signals and in maintaining physiological equilibrium.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Sense Organ Complexity
In frog sensory anatomy, eyes and internal ears are classified as well-organised anatomical organs, whereas touch papillae, taste buds, and olfactory nasal epithelium are merely cellular aggregations around terminal nerve endings. Thus, the proposition inverting these structural designations is factually false.

Step 2: Evaluation of Ear Physiological Roles
The amphibian ear lacks an external pinna; sound is collected by the surface tympanum and transmitted to the internal ear, which acts as a statacoustic organ mediating both auditory reception and balance (equilibrium). Thus, the proposition regarding dual acoustic and equilibrium functions is factually accurate.

Step 3: Final Conceptual Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, but the second statement is correct.
